Amazon provides a dedicated email address for bereavement support requests. Requests require a death certificate and the account's associated email or phone number. (Based on the search result only: the crawler could not read the page itself.)

Apple provides options for loved ones to request access to or delete a deceased person’s Apple Account and associated data after death. Access requires verified legal documentation such as a death certificate or court order, and the process varies by country. Apple also removes Activation Lock automatically after a Legacy Contact request or account deletion is completed.

Coinbase explains how a person named to claim a deceased holder's account can do so through an Executor Services form, submitting a death certificate, probate documents, photo ID and a signed instruction letter. Coinbase does not currently support naming a beneficiary for individual accounts. Estate planning documents or state intestate laws dictate the ownership transfer of the account.

Google says account holders can use Inactive Account Manager to say who should have access to their information and whether the account should be deleted. Google can work with immediate family members and representatives to close a deceased person's account, and may in certain circumstances provide content from it, after careful review. It cannot provide passwords or login details, and users can also submit a request for funds from a deceased user's account.

Dropbox says people who cannot reach the deceased person's Dropbox folder on their computer must request access from Dropbox directly by creating a support ticket. The requester must provide documentation that the person is deceased and that they have a legal right to the files, including government-issued ID and a court order. Dropbox says the process can take time and that it cannot guarantee access.

GitHub allows authorized individuals to request account actions for a deceased user via the Support portal. Requests require details about the deceased, the requester's relationship, and desired action. GitHub may request proof of death and authorization to verify the request.

Google allows immediate family members or representatives to request account closure or content access for a deceased user after a careful review. Inactive Account Manager lets users pre-appoint someone to manage their account if it becomes inactive. Google cannot provide passwords and will not release account contents after closure.

When an insured person dies, their compulsory health insurance ends and premiums are only payable until the date of death, with excess premiums refunded. A partner, close relative or social services case worker can report the death, and a copy of the death certificate is required as proof. If the family contact person on a family contract has died, a new contact person within the family must be named.

Microsoft does not need to be notified of a death; accounts can be closed by someone with the credentials, or are closed automatically after two years of inactivity. Outlook.com and OneDrive accounts are frozen after 1 year and content is deleted shortly after, and subscriptions should be cancelled by stopping payment. Access to content generally requires a subpoena or court order, with documented proof of death and succession for customers in Germany and China.

Netflix says it can help cancel the account of a member who has died, on their behalf. If the person has access, they can use the Cancel Membership link on the Account page and sign out of all devices. If not, they must contact Netflix with the account email or phone number and the full payment information currently used.

PayPal requires the authorised executor or administrator of a deceased person's estate to close the account. The executor must provide specific documentation, including a death certificate and proof of their authority, to bereavement@paypal.com.au. PayPal can disburse remaining funds to a linked bank account or via wire transfer.

Mail addressed to a deceased person can be redirected to another address for a limited time, for example to a relative, until formalities are completed. The redirection can only be requested at a post office branch, not by phone or email, and costs CHF 57.00 for 12 months. Authorities and other contractual partners must be informed of the death separately.

PostFinance asks for a copy of the death certificate and gives information only to legitimate heirs or authorized persons with an official document. The deceased person's PostFinance Card and e-finance accesses are cancelled automatically, and accounts must be closed within 12 months of reporting the death, as no one can take over the account. Existing powers of attorney continue after death, and fees of CHF 30 per quarter apply if the account is not closed within 12 months.

SBB offers a cancellation form for all active travelcards of a person who has died. GA and Half-Fare travelcards are refunded to an IBAN account, while other travelcards are credited to the original payment method. If that is not possible, refunds go via a voucher for sole heirs or to an IBAN account for communities of heirs or government agencies.
none

Swisscom says that after a death the contract can be cancelled immediately at no extra cost, or a mobile, fixed network, internet or TV subscription can be taken over, and a death certificate is needed. For prepaid numbers the remaining credit is transferred automatically on transfer, and the account is deactivated if the number is not used within 12 months. Authorized individuals can request access to the deceased person's email or myCloud using an access request form with a copy of the death certificate.

TalkTalk provides a dedicated bereavement team to assist with account changes or closure after a death. They require the account details and holder's name when contacted. The team is available Monday to Friday 9:00am–7:00pm and Saturday 9:00am–6:00pm.

Anyone can report a client's death to UBS Switzerland, which needs a death certificate and records the death. Heirs take the client's place and must show a certificate of inheritance and identity documents to get information and dispose of assets; executors need an official document. In joint accounts, the surviving contractual partner can usually continue to dispose of the assets individually.
